title: Inside the Standard Library: map
hints: `map` is a generic method on `Sequence`: `Element` in, `T` out.
Loop over `self`, append `try transform(element)`, and mark the method `rethrows`.
jsBridge: Writing `map` yourself shows what JS's `Array.prototype.map` hides: `reserveCapacity(underestimatedCount)` avoids reallocations, `rethrows` propagates errors, and generics keep it type-safe for any `Sequence`.

compass.q: JS `map` exists only on arrays (plus typed arrays). What does writing it on `Sequence` give you?
Why `underestimatedCount` and not `count`? What sequences can't know their count?
